thread:
zoe: Postmortem follow-up for the weekend paging storm. Short goal: assign owners, shrink noise, and lock down a replayable remediation checklist. I spun up a tiny tracker: https://go.redwood/pm-noisechain 

pavan: I'll take owner for threshold tuning on the storage-service alerts. Plan: move to a percentile-based rule, increase `for` to 4m, and add a `warning` vs `page` label. ETA Tue COB. 

e llen: I'll cover dedupe and suppression for shard fanouts. Thinking: `dedupe_key=shard_id` + 8m suppression, then switch to probabilistic dedupe if noise persists. Need 21d alert history to pick exact window. 

rc_oncall_bot: Task created: PM-4577 "Tune storage-service alerts & dedupe" assigned to @pavan and @ellen, due 2026-04-09. 

pavan: Draft rule snippet I'm testing in staging: ```alert: storage_ops_p95 expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(storage_ops_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard)) > 0.4 for: 4m labels: severity: page team: storage annotations: runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/STORAGE-RN``` Will add `owner=pavan` and a rollback snippet. 

ellen: For suppression tests I'll add a replay harness to tracker that simulates 1-2min fanout spikes vs sustained overload. We must ensure suppression doesn't mask real failovers. 

mike: Proposal for paging policy: (1) warning -> slack thread + ticket, no page; (2) page -> page SRE; (3) repeated page (same dedupe key) >2 times in 30m -> escalate to oncall lead. Also disable auto-paging for warning tier while we iterate. 

zoe: Canary plan: enable new rules + dedupe in us-west-2 for 12h, monitor `pages_per_hour`, `tickets_opened`, and `mean_time_to_detect`. If pages drop and detection stays same, roll to other regions. 

pavan: I'll open the PR with new rule + comparison queries and post link here. 

ellen: Added 21d counts and suppression harness to tracker. 

zoe: Owners: pavan (thresholds + PR), ellen (dedupe + suppression harness), mike (paging policy + escalation doc). We'll reconvene in Wed standup to close PM-4577. If you can't hit ETA mark item blocked in the tracker. :white_check_mark:
